result:
I graded submission s1 for quiz 0001 and wrote the grades to `grades/0001-s1.json`. Riley got 2 correct, 2 partial and 2 wrong.

| Item | Verdict | Note |
|---|---|---|
| q1 | Correct | The loop is what makes a system an agent. |
| q2 | Wrong (M4) | The model outputs a tool request. It does not read the calendar itself. |
| q3 | Correct | A step limit is the right safeguard against a stuck loop. |
| q4 | Wrong (M4) | The answer is 4 model calls. The program runs the tools. Riley said the model ran them itself. |
| q5 | Partial | It says the result goes back to the model but not why, which is so the model can pick its next step or write the answer. |
| q6 | Partial (M3) | The first half is right: the model picks from the tool descriptions. The claim that it remembers earlier sessions by itself is wrong. |

M4 is the misconception that the model runs the tools itself. M3 is the one that the model remembers earlier sessions by itself.

The main thing to fix is who does what. The model only writes text, including tool requests. The program runs the tools, feeds results back and saves any memory.

I also wrote a learning record, `learning-records/0003-model-does-not-run-tools-or-remember.md`, and updated `NOTES.md`. s2 is still ungraded.

**Next step:** Riley should draw the loop for the laser cutter question and label each step "model" or "program". Then they should redo q5 with both what happens and why.

Should I grade s2 next, so we can see whether these two misconceptions have cleared?
